solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Tongue of mutant angleworm (3,6)

indicatorNotes.mutant: a mutant has its make-up changed, so the letters of ANGLEWORM are rearranged

blocks.note: ANGLEWORM rearranged, nine letters

annotation.surface: A language spoken by some strange genetically altered earthworm.
annotation.walkthrough: An angleworm is an earthworm used as fishing bait, which makes a talking worm an absurd picture; 'Tongue' is a language, not the organ.
annotation.definitionFit: Low German is the family of German dialects spoken in the flat north of Germany.

entries.clue: Spots something positive in Spanish article (9)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' read as position: one thing sits in another, so CATION goes inside LOS

blocks.note: los is the Spanish plural 'the'
a cation is a positively charged ion

annotation.surface: Someone finding a bright side in a newspaper piece from Spain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spots' looks like a verb, noticing, but it is the plural noun for places. 'Article' here is grammar, a word for 'the'.
annotation.definitionFit: Spots and locations are both places where something is or happens.

entries.clue: Builder uses this with inclination to exclude scrap (11)

blocks.note: W is short for with
a ship's heel is its lean to one side
to bar someone is to exclude them
a scrap and a row are both fights

annotation.surface: A builder who likes to keep scrap metal out of his work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' pretends to be waste material from a building site, but it is a quarrel.
annotation.definitionFit: A wheelbarrow is the one-wheeled cart builders use to move bricks and cement.

entries.clue: Topless groom is finished (5)

indicatorNotes.Topless: the top of a down word is its first letter, so NEATEN loses N

blocks.note: to groom is to tidy, to neaten
drop the first letter N

annotation.surface: A bridegroom caught without a shirt is done for.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Groom' is a verb, to tidy, not the man at the altar.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the food sense: once every plate is cleared, the dinner is finished.

entries.clue: Steep ruin in boundless sea? (8)

indicatorNotes.boundless: without its bounds, its outer letters, WATER becomes ATE

blocks.note: to mar something is to spoil it
used as it stands
the sea is water, hence the question mark
WATER loses W and R, leaving ATE

annotation.surface: A shipwreck left to soak in the endless ocean.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Steep' reads as an adjective for a cliff, but it is the verb, to soak.
annotation.definitionFit: To marinate food is to steep it in a liquid to flavour it.

entries.clue: Failing in duty, being out of habit (6)

indicatorNotes.Failing: something failing goes wrong, so IN DUTY is rearranged

blocks.note: IN DUTY rearranged, six letters

annotation.surface: Someone neglecting their obligations because they have fallen out of routine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out of habit' sounds like losing a routine; a habit is also a nun's robe, so being out of it means wearing nothing.
annotation.definitionFit: Nudity is the state of wearing no clothes, being out of one's habit in the garment sense.

entries.clue: Queen replaces ring out of insincere fault-finding (13)

indicatorNotes.replaces: to replace something is to take its place, so the queen's letters stand where the ring's letter stood
indicatorNotes.out of: the new word is made out of HYPOCRITICAL

blocks.note: hypocritical = insincere
O is round like a ring; it comes out
ER = Elizabeth Regina; it goes in where O was

annotation.surface: A monarch swapping a wedding ring for criticism that is not sincere.
annotation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is a standard way to clue a queen.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone hypercritical finds fault with everything, far more than is reasonable.

entries.clue: Roman’s here to collect river aggregate that’s brought up — it might encourage movement (5,5)

indicatorNotes.to collect: HIC collects the other letters, so they go inside it
indicatorNotes.brought up: in a down answer, brought up means turned to read bottom to top, so SUM becomes MUS

blocks.note: hic is Latin for here
the Ouse is a Yorkshire river
an aggregate is a SUM, turned round

annotation.surface: A Roman gathering river gravel dredged up, which might keep things flowing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Aggregate' pretends to be gravel beside a river, but it is a total. The movement encouraged is dancing.
annotation.definitionFit: House music is electronic dance music with a steady beat, made to get people moving.

entries.clue: The ploy began to unravel in storage unit? (9,3)

indicatorNotes.to unravel: what unravels comes apart, so THE PLOY BEGAN is rearranged

blocks.note: THE PLOY BEGAN rearranged, twelve letters

annotation.surface: A scheme that fell apart in a self-storage warehouse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Storage unit' suggests a rented lock-up; the question mark admits it is only a plastic bag.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example with a wink: a plastic sack holds things, so it counts as somewhere to store them, if not a rented lock-up.

entries.clue: Give another name to About Time, displayed in part of wall (7)

indicatorNotes.displayed in: T is shown in TILE, so it sits inside it

blocks.note: re = about, as in a letter heading
a tile is part of a tiled wall
T = time

annotation.surface: Someone suggesting a new name for the film About Time, shown on a wall.
annotation.walkthrough: About Time is a real film, so the capitals make it look like a title to be renamed; it splits into RE and T.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the RE- prefix means again, so the word is literally to title once more.

entries.clue: Thoughtlessly approving tips, barmen struggling with grub (6-8)

indicatorNotes.struggling: struggling things are thrown about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, ten letters
anagram fodder, four letters

annotation.surface: Bar staff happily accepting gratuities while battling to serve food.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Approving tips' reads as barmen welcoming gratuities, but 'Thoughtlessly approving' is the definition and 'tips' is just fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: To rubber-stamp is to approve something automatically, without real scrutiny.

entries.clue: Repeatedly bring forward anti-Communist slogan? (4,3)

blocks.note: the idiom for producing the same tired excuse or argument yet again
a chant demanding the removal of a Trotskyist, split into two words

annotation.surface: A politician forever wheeling out the same slogan against the Reds.
annotation.walkthrough: A Trot is a nickname for a Trotskyist, a hard-left Communist; the question mark flags the made-up slogan.
annotation.definitionFit: To trot out an argument is to bring it out again, as one has many times before.

entries.clue: Hoax certificate — good idea for prom attendee? (11)

blocks.note: a con is a trick
cert is short for certificate
a goer is a plan that will work

annotation.surface: A forged ticket, which seems a clever plan for someone going to the school prom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prom' suggests an American school dance; in Britain the Proms are a summer season of classical concerts in London.
annotation.definitionFit: Anyone attending a Prom concert is a concertgoer.

entries.clue: Song including introduction to Devil Woman (4)

indicatorNotes.including: LAY includes D, so D sits inside
indicatorNotes.introduction to: an introduction comes first, so take the first letter of Devil

blocks.note: a lay is an old word for a song
first letter of Devil

annotation.surface: A song whose opening features the hit Devil Woman.
annotation.walkthrough: Devil Woman is a real Cliff Richard song, which makes the phrase look like one title; it splits, with 'Woman' the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A lady is a woman, especially a polite or refined one.

entries.clue: Where Labour is following Conservative split (5)

indicatorNotes.following: LEFT follows C, so it comes after it

blocks.note: C = Conservative, the British party
the Labour Party sits on the political left

annotation.surface: A political commentator describing Labour trailing behind a divided Tory party.
annotation.walkthrough: Labour and the Conservatives are Britain's two main parties, on the left and right. 'Split' is the definition, not a party squabble.
annotation.definitionFit: Cleft is a past form of cleave, meaning split apart.

entries.clue: Friends regularly do fish (3,6)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals: every second letter of Friends

blocks.note: the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of fRiEnDs
a do is a hairdo, and a mullet is one

annotation.surface: Friends who often cook fish together.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Do' pretends to be a verb, but it is a hairstyle; the mullet is short at the front and long at the back.
annotation.definitionFit: The red mullet is a reddish Mediterranean fish prized for eating.

entries.clue: Former train managers had been in The Sun (7)

blocks.note: BR = British Rail, which ran Britain's trains until the 1990s
had = owned, possessed

annotation.surface: Ex-railway bosses who were once written up in the tabloid newspaper The Sun.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals make The Sun look like the tabloid, but it is the sun that tans you. 'Had' does double work in the surface: 'had browned' reads as 'had been in the sun'.
annotation.definitionFit: Skin that has browned has been tanned by time in the sun.

entries.clue: At first the zoo hadn’t let in teen, keen to cook rabbit (4,8,2,3,5)

indicatorNotes.to cook: to cook is to mix up, so the letters are rearranged

anagram.fodder: T ZOO HADNT LET IN TEEN KEEN

blocks.note: first letter of 'the'

blocks.clueFragment: zoo hadn’t let in teen, keen
blocks.note: anagram fodder, 21 letters, ignoring the apostrophe

annotation.surface: A keen teenager turned away by a zoo, wanting to cook a rabbit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' sits at the end looking like the thing cooked, but it is British slang for chatter, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' for talk.
annotation.definitionFit: To talk nineteen to the dozen is to chatter nonstop, which is what rabbiting on means.

entries.clue: Horror movie exam papers getting recalled (8)

indicatorNotes.recalled: called back, so ET SATS ID is read backwards

blocks.note: E.T. is Spielberg's alien film
SATs are national school tests in England, and the US college test
ID = identity papers

annotation.surface: A horror film whose exam papers are being withdrawn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Horror movie' reads as one phrase, but 'Horror' is the definition on its own and the movie is E.T., hardly scary.
annotation.definitionFit: Distaste is a feeling of dislike or mild horror at something.

entries.clue: Love to sleep at night in such a way as to be picked up with minimal effort (2,1,5)

annotation.definition: in such a way as to be picked up with minimal effort

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, and zero looks like O
to nap is to sleep briefly
late = at night, well into the evening

annotation.surface: Someone who loves a nap late at night, done so easily it is as if they were carried to bed.
annotation.walkthrough: The long definition describes something handed over so easily it could be lifted off a dish.
annotation.definitionFit: To get something on a plate is to get it without having to work for it.

entries.clue: Constancy of prince perhaps shaking head between two lochs (9)

indicatorNotes.shaking head: shaking off its head, ROYAL loses its first letter
indicatorNotes.between: OYAL goes between L and NESS

blocks.note: L = loch, the first of the two
a prince is an example of a royal
ROYAL loses R, leaving OYAL
Loch Ness, the second loch

annotation.surface: A prince shaking his head while standing between two Scottish lakes.
annotation.walkthrough: A loch is a Scottish lake. The two lochs are clued differently: one is the abbreviation L, the other is Loch Ness by name.
annotation.definitionFit: Loyalness is faithfulness, being constant to someone.

entries.clue: Harsh and tense, except if swallowing tablet (8)

indicatorNotes.swallowing: UNLESS swallows E, so E goes inside

blocks.note: T = tense, in grammar
unless = except if
E = ecstasy, a tablet

annotation.surface: Someone harsh and on edge, unless they have taken a pill.
annotation.walkthrough: The tablet is an E, slang for an ecstasy pill. 'Harsh' here means grating on the ear.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym in the musical sense: singing without melody grates on the ear, and harsh describes that sound.

entries.clue: African expresses annoyance with India (5)

blocks.note: to tut is to click the tongue in disapproval
India is I in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: An African who is irritated with India.
annotation.walkthrough: TUTS is the sound of a click of the tongue, written as a verb; the clue's plain surface hides little else.
annotation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are a people of Rwanda and Burundi in central Africa.

entries.clue: Send down, say, in recount (8)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' read as position: one thing placed in another, so EG goes inside RELATE

blocks.note: to relate a story is to recount it
e.g. = say, for example

annotation.surface: A demand to throw someone out, for instance during a vote recount.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recount' suggests counting votes again, but it means telling a story. In British football, relegated teams go down a division.
annotation.definitionFit: To relegate is to send down to a lower rank or division.

entries.clue: Cats perhaps way ahead of fish (6)

indicatorNotes.ahead of: to be ahead of something is to be in front of it, so the way's letters come before the fish's

blocks.note: St = street, a way
rays are flat fish

annotation.surface: Cats heading for a fish supper.
annotation.walkthrough: ST, for street, is the usual crossword way to turn 'way' into letters. 'Cats perhaps' is a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: Stray cats are homeless animals, and 'perhaps' admits dogs can be strays too.

entries.clue: Lust of French father (6)

blocks.note: de is French for of
to sire is to father; a sire is a father

annotation.surface: The lust of a French father.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of French' tells you to translate 'of' into French rather than to describe the father as French.
annotation.definitionFit: Desire and lust are both strong wanting, often sexual.

entries.clue: Take time — what Olympics chief did? (9)

blocks.note: T = time
the head of the Olympics ran sport

annotation.surface: A plea to slow down, with a question about the Olympic boss's job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take time' reads as one phrase, but 'Take' is the definition alone; 'ran' also nods to athletes running.
annotation.definitionFit: To transport people or goods is to take them somewhere.

entries.clue: Dish of eastern European butter, maybe on the counter (8)

indicatorNotes.on the counter: to run counter is to go the opposite way, so E DANE PAT is reversed

blocks.note: E = eastern
a Dane is a European, hence 'maybe'
a pat of butter

annotation.surface: A Polish or Hungarian butter dish sitting on the kitchen counter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Counter' pretends to be a kitchen worktop, but 'on the counter' means going the contrary way.
annotation.definitionFit: Tapenade is a Provençal dish, a paste of olives, capers and anchovies.

entries.clue: Main quality of points covered by short dance (9)

indicatorNotes.covered by: TINES is covered by SALS, so it sits inside
indicatorNotes.short: cut short, SALSA loses its last letter

blocks.note: SALSA, a Latin dance, loses its last letter
tines are the points of a fork or antler

annotation.surface: A dance teacher's main concern: pointing the toes in a quick routine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like chief, but the main is the sea, whose quality is salt.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: 'the main' is an old poetic word for the open sea, and salt is what sets sea water apart.

entries.clue: Significance of where snow isn’t shifting south (14)

indicatorNotes.shifting: things that shift move about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters, ignoring the apostrophe
S = south, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A weather report on the importance of the places where snow is absent, moving south.
annotation.walkthrough: 'South' reads as the direction the weather is moving, but it only adds one S to the letters being rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: Newsworthiness is the significance that makes an event worth reporting.

entries.clue: English comedic actor filling berth at sea (10)

indicatorNotes.filling: E WILDER fills BED, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a berth is a bed on a ship
E = English
Gene Wilder, star of Young Frankenstein

annotation.surface: An English comic squeezed into a bunk on a ship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Berth' and 'at sea' paint a voyage, but 'at sea' means confused.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone at sea is bewildered, lost and confused.

entries.clue: Friend initially doesn’t mind about his faith (8)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the initial letters of 'doesn't mind'
indicatorNotes.about: 'about' read as around: D and M sit on either side of HIS, surrounding it

blocks.note: bud = buddy, a friend
first letters of Doesn't and Mind
used as it stands, inside D…M

annotation.surface: A tolerant friend who is relaxed about his mate's religion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Initially' reads as if it belongs to 'Friend', but it works on the two words after it.
annotation.definitionFit: Buddhism is the faith founded on the teachings of the Buddha.

entries.clue: Complain about accent (4)

blocks.note: ca. = circa, about
RP = Received Pronunciation, the standard British accent

annotation.surface: Someone moaning about the way another person speaks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a link to 'accent', but it is the wordplay CA.
annotation.definitionFit: To carp is to complain in a petty, nagging way.

entries.clue: Star related to the sun not initially accepted by irrational figures (7)

indicatorNotes.not initially: without its initial letter, SOLAR becomes OLAR
indicatorNotes.accepted by: OLAR is taken in by PIS, so it goes inside

blocks.note: pi is an irrational number; two of them are pis
solar = of the sun
SOLAR loses S, leaving OLAR

annotation.surface: A star linked to the sun that unreasonable people will not accept.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Irrational figures' sounds like unreasonable people, but the figures are numbers like pi.
annotation.definitionFit: Polaris is the Pole Star, above the North Pole.

entries.clue: Sports drill AI composed, embraced by Spurs (3,9)

annotation.definitionNote: BAR BILLIARDS is one game, but its name ends in S, so it can stand for a plural-looking 'Sports'

indicatorNotes.composed: to compose is to arrange, so DRILL AI is rearranged
indicatorNotes.embraced by: BARBS embraces the result, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a spur and a barb are both sharp points
DRILL AI rearranged, going inside BARB…S

annotation.surface: An AI writing training exercises, backed by the football club Spurs.
annotation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, the London football club; here it means barbs. Bar billiards is a table game played in British pubs.
annotation.definitionFit: Bar billiards is a pub game played on a small table with holes in its surface.

entries.clue: They fly upward as her seaplane circles (7)

indicatorNotes.circles: the phrase circles the answer, holding it inside

blocks.note: inside upwarD AS HER Seaplane

annotation.surface: A woman's seaplane circling as it climbs, with birds flying up alongside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upward' looks like the direction of flight, but it holds the first letter of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Dashers are people who dash, and to fly is to dash off in a hurry.

entries.clue: Reach a part of Anfield, one much appreciated for continental food (11)

blocks.note: a span is a reach or stretch
used as it stands
the Kop is the famous stand at Anfield, Liverpool's football ground
I = one, the Roman numeral
ta is British slang for thanks

annotation.surface: A Liverpool fan grateful for European food at the stadium.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface places you at a football ground; the food is Greek, which 'continental' covers as mainland Europe from a British point of view.
annotation.definitionFit: Spanakopita is a Greek pie of spinach and feta in filo pastry.

entries.clue: First-class Berliner’s agreed with Times hero (4)

blocks.note: A = first-class, as in A1
ja is German for yes
X is the times sign in multiplication

annotation.surface: A top German agreeing with the Times newspaper about a hero.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Times' pretends to be this newspaper, but it is multiplication.
annotation.definitionFit: Ajax was a Greek hero of the Trojan War.

entries.clue: Painful, backward Mediterranean island: one’s taking on new Cypriot character (10)

indicatorNotes.backward: the whole string ELBA IVNE NU is read backward
indicatorNotes.taking on: IVE takes on N, holding it inside

blocks.note: Elba, where Napoleon was exiled
one has = I have = I've
N = new, inside IVE
nu is a Greek letter, and Greek is written in Cyprus

annotation.surface: A dismal island going downhill, one person picking up a new Cypriot figure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backward' seems to belong to the island alone, but it turns the whole chain round. 'One's' has to be read as 'one has', giving I'VE.
annotation.definitionFit: An unenviable position is a painful or difficult one that nobody would want.

entries.clue: Second crown put back on monarch going on holiday? (11)

indicatorNotes.put back: put back to front, CAP becomes PAC

blocks.note: to second a motion is to back it
a crown is a CAP, turned round
a king is a monarch; PAC goes on it

annotation.surface: A crown being replaced on a king's head before he sets off on holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that backpacking is only one kind of holiday.
annotation.definitionFit: Backpacking is cheap travel with everything carried in a pack on the back.

entries.clue: Working with money to infiltrate intelligence, not primarily showing cohesion (10)

indicatorNotes.not primarily: without its first letter, ACUITY becomes CUITY

blocks.note: acuity = sharpness of mind
ACUITY loses A, leaving CUITY
a machine that is on is working
tin is old British slang for money

annotation.surface: A spy paid to get inside the intelligence services, not showing much team spirit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence' suggests spies, but it means sharpness of mind.
annotation.definitionFit: Continuity is unbroken connection, the quality of holding together.

entries.clue: Incorrect dates inscribed into perfect monument (9)

indicatorNotes.Incorrect: incorrect letters are out of order, so DATES is rearranged
indicatorNotes.inscribed into: the rearranged letters are cut into HONE, going inside

blocks.note: to hone a skill is to perfect it
DATES rearranged, going inside H…ONE

annotation.surface: The wrong dates carved on a flawless memorial.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: headstones carry the dates of a life, and a mistake in them would be carved in stone.
annotation.definitionFit: A headstone is a stone monument set at the head of a grave.

entries.clue: Fair and square to take days tracking British Library (6)

indicatorNotes.to take: to take something in is to hold it, so ONE holds D inside
indicatorNotes.tracking: to track is to follow, so ONDE comes after BL

blocks.note: BL = British Library
from 'square one', the starting point
d = days

annotation.surface: A plea for an honest, fair process that takes days to follow the British Library.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fair and square' reads as one idiom, but 'Fair' is the definition alone and 'square' becomes ONE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for hair colour: fair and blonde both describe light, yellowish hair.

entries.clue: Old jazz fan and policeman featuring in magazine (6)

indicatorNotes.featuring in: PC features in HEAT, so it goes inside

blocks.note: Heat is a British celebrity magazine
PC = police constable

annotation.surface: A retired jazz lover and a police officer both appearing in a magazine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old' belongs to the definition: the word is dated slang from the swing era, not a description of an elderly fan.
annotation.definitionFit: Hepcat is 1940s slang for a hip jazz enthusiast.

entries.clue: Bed ready with this firstly positioned? (5,4)

annotation.definition: Bed ready with this firstly positioned?

indicatorNotes.positioned: the letters are put into new positions, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, eight letters
first letter of 'this'

annotation.surface: A bed is only ready once this has been placed on it.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a child's bed isn't ready until the teddy is in place.
annotation.definitionFit: A teddy bear is the soft toy often placed on a child's bed.

entries.clue: Where elders may be rendered in sculpture, perhaps American (8)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' read as position: one thing set in another, so BORE goes inside ART A

blocks.note: sculpture is an example of art
A = American
bore = yielded or gave, as in 'bore fruit'

annotation.walkthrough: 'Elders' suggests old people, but elders are trees, and arboreta are where trees are grown.
annotation.definitionFit: Arboreta, plural of arboretum, are collections of trees, including elders.

entries.clue: Small river rod (5)

blocks.note: S = small, as in clothing sizes
the Taff is a Welsh river that runs through Cardiff

annotation.surface: A little fishing rod for a stream.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Small river' looks like a stream to fish in, but the two words give separate pieces.

entries.clue: Briefly cover S&M ideology (7)

used as it stands

annotation.walkthrough: 'Cover' is a noun here, a panel or facing, not the verb to hide.

entries.clue: Gallery carrying advanced volume, abridged to order (8)

indicatorNotes.carrying: TATE carries A BUL inside it

A = advanced, as in A level
BULK = volume, losing its last letter

entries.clue: He might not let you enter ball? (7)

annotation.definition: He might not let you enter

blocks.clueFragment: He might not let you enter
blocks.note: a doorman who turns people away
in cricket, a short-pitched delivery that rears up at the batter

blocks.note: a single was often released on CD
rash = impulsive
one's old man is one's father, pa

s = succeeded

entries.clue: Catholic nuns may not riot, having resettled in Monaco? (14,8)

annotation.walkthrough: The question mark shows Monaco is just one example of this kind of state.

entries.clue: A key passage (5)

a key or cay is a low island, as in the Florida Keys

entries.clue: Opinion on husband’s letter from Jerusalem (4)

H = husband; BET goes on it

annotation.surface: A view on a husband's letter sent from Jerusalem.

entries.clue: Journalist provided with cool building of impressive size (7)

to ice is to cool

annotation.surface: A reporter given a cool office in a huge building.
annotation.walkthrough: ED, for editor, is the standard crossword journalist.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word comes from Latin for building and now suggests something grand.

entries.clue: Trolley that is carrying insulation tissue (9)

indicatorNotes.carrying: to carry something is to hold it, so IE holds LAG inside

blocks.note: a cart is a trolley
i.e. = that is
to lag pipes is to insulate them

annotation.surface: A trolley loaded with insulating tissue paper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tissue' suggests paper, but it is body tissue.
annotation.definitionFit: Cartilage is the tough, flexible connective tissue in joints, ears and nose.

entries.clue: Initially Spider-Man’s peer, is that Eddie or Venom? (5)

indicatorNotes.Initially: take the initial letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: first letters of Spider-Man's, Peer, Is, That, Eddie

annotation.surface: A comic fan asking whether Spider-Man's rival is Eddie Brock or the monster Venom.
annotation.walkthrough: In Marvel comics Eddie Brock becomes the villain Venom, so 'Eddie or Venom' looks like one question; 'Venom' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Spite is malice, the venom of someone wishing harm.

entries.clue: Thrilling to hide bit on the side of Miss Trunchbull? (13)

blocks.note: heady = exciting, intoxicating
a bit on the side is a secret lover

annotation.surface: Excitement about a secret affair of the fearsome Miss Trunchbull.
annotation.walkthrough: Miss Trunchbull is the tyrannical headmistress in Roald Dahl's Matilda, so the idea of her having a lover is absurd.
annotation.definitionFit: Headmistressy means stern and bossy, like a formidable headmistress such as Miss Trunchbull.

entries.clue: Lion King villain adopting very English energy for hyena? (9)

indicatorNotes.adopting: SCAR adopts V ENG E, taking them inside

blocks.note: Scar is the villainous lion in The Lion King
v = very
Eng = English
E = energy

annotation.surface: The Lion King's villain taking on English energy for his hyena henchmen.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: in the film Scar recruits the hyenas as his henchmen.
annotation.definitionFit: Hyenas are scavengers, feeding on the leftovers of others' kills; the question mark marks them as an example.
